# Use tool-use-schema-writer

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Takes a function description (name, purpose, parameters) and writes a valid Anthropic tool_use JSON schema, with type annotations, required fields, and a description for each parameter. Adds a Python client.messages.create(tools=[...]) snippet only when asked.

**Reach for it when** wiring a Claude agent to a function or API, designing tools for a multi-agent system, or documenting an existing tool for agent consumption.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install tool-use-schema-writer                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install tool-use-schema-writer --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install tool-use-schema-writer --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the API builder pack: [`--pack api-builder`](../packs/use-the-api-builder-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Write the tool_use JSON schema for this function so Claude can call it"
- "Turn this TypeScript API client method into an Anthropic tool definition"
- "I have three functions for my agent — write their tool schemas so the model picks the right one"
- "Document this existing endpoint as a tool the agent can consume, with required fields"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Design the control loop for my tool-using agent — stop conditions and retries"
- "Split this workflow across an orchestrator and specialist subagents"
- "Draft the OpenAPI contract for our new public REST API"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use tool-use-schema-writer".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Descriptions are decision conditions, not function names restated.** `"Gets the weather"` is not a description — `"Returns the current temperature and conditions for a given city. Call this when the user asks about current weather, not forecasts."` is.
- **Required arrays are never omitted.** An omitted `required` array means all fields are optional — the model will skip fields the function actually needs and the call will fail at runtime.
- **Enum values always have descriptions.** `"enum": ["asc", "desc"]` without a description leaves the model guessing which to use.
